result.delta_one_sentence: A keeps the tasks, instructions, checkers and OS shell fixed in English and changes only interface text language and layout direction, independently, in one checked config file, so the right-to-left effect splits into additive text and layout parts with intervals and a reachable equivalence null; B localizes the whole OS and the instructions at once, so it can only observe an untested drop and guess at its cause.
result.reasoning: Both designs study one phenomenon: computer-use agents may do worse when the interface is localized right-to-left. The mechanisms differ. B is a broad observational benchmark (about 200 tasks, 30 apps, 5 languages, 6 agents, one run per cell). In its right-to-left condition, script, translated strings, mirrored layout, OS shell localization and (in the matched condition) instruction language all change together. It offers two candidate causes, the visual complexity of the script and the mirrored layout, but has no condition that separates them. It reports no intervals or significance tests, even though the gap is small (13.7% vs 19.3%) and each cell has one run. A is a controlled factorial intervention aimed at exactly the question B leaves open. A 2x2 of text language by layout direction is set by one system file, and everything else is held fixed. It adds pre-run oracles that each switch does only its job: chrome mirrors and documents do not, window titles stay identical, translated strings that leak into documents (such as the default sheet name) are pinned so checkers are not broken by translation, and pixel boxes replace unreliable accessibility boxes under mirroring. It runs a census of eligible tasks with no selection on agent success, repeats episodes across two scaffolds, and decomposes the total change exactly into the two main effects. Its primary decision uses a dual equivalence margin, with simulated power for both a robustness null and a 15% relative harm, plus moderators that test which route carries any effect. A is the stronger causal contribution: a null or a clean attribution from A is interpretable, and B's numbers are not. A's weaknesses are external validity and ecological realism. It covers one office suite, one right-to-left language, an English OS shell and two scaffolds. The Arabic-text-in-left-to-right cell is not a configuration real users see. Its moderators are correlational. B's strengths are breadth, a reusable multi-app, multi-language resource and a separate safety subset, but as evidence about why right-to-left hurts agents it adds little beyond a plausible hypothesis and an anecdote. Net: A tests B's guess with a design that can actually support or reject it, so A is the stronger research contribution on this question. B is the wider benchmark.

Feasibility.lens: Feasibility: is the first step's pilot decisive, and can the step run on 8xH100 within its budget using the assets that exist today?
Feasibility.strongest_argument:
The first step is Phase 0. Its job is to decide the gates K0 (at least 62 tasks admitted) and K1 (the D53 delta certification, P0.6). The pilot that ran cannot decide either gate, and the run that could decide them cannot start with the assets that exist.

Why the pilot does not decide K0 or K1:
- No real Arabic string was ever rendered. In the 106-task sweep (jobs 1099/1100) the "pseudo-Arabic" cell L4 had no catalogs, so its strings fell back to English (compute/pilot/s2v3_pilot_b.py lines 13-14). That cell is English text in a mirrored layout.
- The ar-LTR cell, one of the four Phase 1 cells, never ran at any task state. It ran only on blank documents (L5 in job 1098).
- The pilot ran in the LO-VM container, not in the VM lane on a derived image.
- The registered oracle was not implemented: no O2 ink identity, no O3 on ink-located boxes, no O6, no positive controls, no mirror specification.
  - O3 on AT-SPI was abandoned: job 1100 found 53% of matched elements keep unmirrored extents.
  - O5 was "not claimed". At residual < 0.02 more documents matched the flipped image (34) than the unflipped one (15) (job1099/pilot-b-analysis.json).
- Even the switch location differs from the registered one. The pilot inserted its own xcsxcu layer after the res: layer (job1098/pilot-record.json, prepare.fundamentalrc_after). The registration writes the selector into /etc/libreoffice/registry, which is the same layer as main.xcd.

Why the decisive run cannot start:
- It needs three package downloads. That is an outward action waiting on Kevin.
- It needs image-surgery code that is not written or reviewed.
- It needs a lane version that accepts a new image digest and the 27 reserve tasks (lane.py:90 pins QCOW2_SHA256; line 253 allows only pool and dev tasks).
- It needs a registered deviation of q2-action-path-v2 for P0.6, which does not exist.
- It needs a way to give each VM its own cell, and none exists or is designed. The VM container bind-mounts one pinned qcow2 read-only per manifest (harness/q2/vm/driver.py:133). The four cells "assigned to VM slots at random" therefore need either four images or a runtime write to /etc as root in the guest, through the guest server that D53 does not certify. The registration also needs LANGUAGE=ar in the Arabic cells' LibreOffice process (P0.3). That has no mechanism and contradicts "the cells differ only in one selector file". Neither gap is listed among the proposal's blockers.

By the gauntlet's compute rule the pilot is also not an orx node, so it does not count as an executable pilot and the 79 cap binds.

Phase 1's fit under 8 GPU-h rests on a cap rule nobody has adopted. Under S1a's registered c_proj the same 1,696 episodes are 19.1 GPU-h (registration lines 431-432). The design study (section 5) says "A successor registration needs that rule adopted", and D22 says expected use never replaces a cap. The Phase 1 manifest does not exist and has no dry run (proposal line 400; doctor: "compute lacks a hashed Slurm manifest", "slurm_test did not pass").

The owner's own forecast puts reaching Phase 1 at 0.6 x 0.65 x 0.85, about 0.33.
Feasibility.what_would_change_my_mind:
All of the following would change my verdict:
